text:
devin: heads-up — on a couple dedicated nodes i'm seeing steady RSS creep during long-context replay (200k tokens). not heap leak, looks like KV slot churn + tiny fragments piling up.

maria: can you paste the top lines from /proc/pid/smaps or a samprof of the kv arena?

devin: posted samprof output, but tl;dr: freepool has lots of 32B and 64B free fragments, allocator keeps handing out new 64B blocks instead of reusing slightly-larger holes.

anuj: that matches the microgap issue we saw in canary — allocator split policy is biasing toward exact-fit instead of best-fit for small buckets. leads to many tiny unusable gaps when long-context shifts KV sizes.

maria: paste of pmap snippet: 
```
AnonHugePages: 0 kB
Rss: 2349216 kB
... kv_arena: 1.1GB (active blocks ~ 17k)
small_free_32: 4.2k
small_free_64: 2.8k
```

samir: quick thought: we tuned blocksize to 64/core to reduce TLB churn, but that makes small object fragmentation worse if reuse window is skewed. maybe try mixed bin sizes (power-of-two + intermediate 48B) for hot lanes.

devin: i ran a micro with modified allocator: added a 48B bucket and changed split threshold so a 64B hole will be used for 96B request after coalescing. results look promising — memory creep slowed by ~45% over 6h replay. perf-bot posted diffs:

perf-bot: regression-checker: perf change on dedicated-24gpu: p99 latency +0.2%, throughput -0.6%, memory growth rate -44% on long-context workload.

anuj: good. what's the tradeoff for latency? extra coalesce scanning could add contention on hot paths. did you gate coalesce behind sampling?

devin: yes — we only trigger coalesce in allocator on miss if free list length > threshold and on background scrub thread for cold buckets. coalesce incremental and bounded (~128 ops/s).

maria: can you share the config patch? I'd like to run the daily stability job. also add a tracepoint for "kv:coalesce:scan_len=%d:merged=%d"

devin: config snippet pasted: 
```
kv_allocator:
  enable_incremental_coalesce: true
  coalesce_scan_budget: 128
  tiny_buckets: [16,32,48,64]
  split_threshold: 0.6
  sample_rate: 0.01
```

samir: we should also consider a gentle compaction scheduler that prioritizes buckets by fragmentation score *and* expected future reuse (based on prefix reuse histogram). i can sketch heuristic: score = frag_ratio * (1 - reuse_prob).

anuj: +1. also add a burst-safe path: when batching heuristics cause many similar seq-length requests, temporarily bias allocations toward fewer larger blocks to improve KV reuse (reduces per-token KV misses).

maria: ran stability job with patch — 24h run looks green, small regression in tail but within SLA. posting trace excerpt: 
```
kv:coalesce:scan_len=94:merged=28
kv:alloc:hot_reuse_hit=0.62
kv:free_frag_ratio=0.18
```

perf-bot: regression-checker: extended run: p99 +0.15%, memory-growth delta -40%, token cost -2.1% (good).

devin: next steps: 1) converge on bucket sizes (48 seems best so far), 2) add frag-score based compaction scheduler, 3) roll patch to canary and monitor TTL workloads for edge cases.

ops-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 2026-03-20T02:00:00Z (rolling, 5% capacity). alert if kv_free_frag_ratio > 0.25 for >30m.

maria: i'll follow up with a short RFC for the coalesce scheduler (heuristics + telemetry) and add the tracepoints. thanks all :thumbsup:
